summary:

Long-duration spaceflight presents unique challenges to human health, including the effects of microgravity, space radiation, isolation, and limited access to medical assistance. We aim to help address these challenges through technology.

By collecting and analyzing this information, AxoMed aims to identify unusual patterns, detect potential health issues, and generate timely alerts. 
Crews can log daily check-ins, manage a 2-month pills and countermeasure calendar, and keep a private crew diary.
A standout feature is Dr. Axo, a friendly chibi axolotl companion that surfaces anomaly alerts, explains why spaceflight issues occur, and presents evidence-backed countermeasures in a friendly and approachable way. 
Through an intuitive dashboard, astronauts can access relevant health information on board (and optionally export health telemetry when needed) and make better-informed decisions.
AxoMed aims to contribute to safer space missions by making astronaut health monitoring more proactive, accessible, and human-centered.
details:
AxoMed is a visual prototype of an autonomous astronaut health monitoring dashboard designed to support crew members during deep-space missions. Space environments expose astronauts to challenges such as microgravity, space radiation, isolation, communication delays, and limited access to medical assistance. Our project aims to make health monitoring more proactive, and human-centered.

Using a 30-day synthetic mission dataset modeled after NASA OSDR (Inspiration4), NASA HRP, and CSA research, the platform tracks physiological and psychological indicators across five body systems—heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, HRV, sleep, cognitive reaction speed, blood hemoglobin, hydration/renal markers, skin temperature, and radiation exposure. By comparing health data with individual baselines, AxoMed identifies unusual patterns and generates timely alerts when potential health concerns arise. This information is presented through an intuitive, interactive body-map dashboard, allowing astronauts to follow health indicators autonomously on board and optionally export health telemetry (separately from private notes) when needed.

In addition to telemetry trends, crews can log daily check-ins (including a live cognitive reaction timer), manage a 2-month pills and countermeasure calendar with active dose alerts, and keep a strictly private crew diary.
One of AxoMed's most distinctive features is Dr. Axo, a friendly chibi axolotl companion. In this prototype, Dr. Axo uses research-backed triage rules to communicate alerts, explain why spaceflight issues occur, and present evidence- based countermeasures in a warm, approachable way. We believe this system—and any future AI integrated into it—should run 100% locally on board to ensure zero-latency support and complete crew privacy.
The project offers several benefits: centralized onboard health information, personalized baseline monitoring, earlier awareness of potential health risks, private mental-health journaling, and clearer communication of alerts. Its intended impact is to contribute to astronaut safety and well-being, especially during long-duration missions where immediate Earth medical assistance is not available.

AxoMed combines software development, data visualization, and space-medicine research. Our creativity lies in pairing clinical spaceflight telemetry with an interactive companion mascot and calming neumorphic design to give the platform a more human and engaging approach. AI coding assistants were used to help with React/TypeScript implementation and debugging, create the synthetic dataset and diary entries, and edit documentation.

Ultimately, AxoMed seeks to support healthier astronauts and safer space exploration through thoughtful, local-first design.

SpaceX Inspiration4 Blood Serum Metabolic Panel and Immune/Cardiac Cytokine Arrays (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Multiplex)
SpaceX Inspiration4 Urine Inflammation Panel (Multiplex, NULISAseq)
